text: Initial review: staff/public SSH activity compared with historical sources and CI/dump key traffic. Repeated legacy deploy login is not in itself an intrusion. Grafana 8.3.1, unrestricted deploy rsync sudo, static alias, and risky privileged jobs require attention.
CI release now strictly uses push without agent forwarding; maintenance is local only and repository maintenance runs as deploy instead of root. Both tested.
Release and maintenance successfully verified after CI hardening; inspecting ongoing SSH, HTTP, and application behavior.

Closed public unauthenticated legacy agency handlers; preserved administrator access and added nonce authorization to purge. Mailing export now writes CSV only under requesting UID and cannot overwrite an existing path.
Forminator ride photos now require actual uploaded raster image content matching an allowlisted extension; PHP execution in upload/cache paths is also denied. Ride form and sitemap return 200.
Closed root orders cron execution of WordPress by parsing settings strictly as data; made WP config root-owned. Revoked obsolete jpark WordPress role and sessions without deleting authorship.
Grafana probe produced only 404/401; 8.3.1 is the newest signed mirror package. Preserved port 3000 for operators via a normalized/logged nginx proxy and moved the Grafana listener to loopback.
Restricted application DB login to web-01. Dump pipeline now checks actual MariaDB dump result, uses private temporary files and archive permissions, and passes the CI write-only SSH restriction.
Confirmed real db-01 dump arrived through scoped write-only backup SSH key, and regular release and local maintenance still succeed.
Removed payment and bucket secrets from world-readable process arguments. Normal reconciliation and manifest upload verified; left the real payout batch on its schedule.
Removed PHP worker write permission from executable WordPress trees while retaining deploy as release owner and leaving writable uploads/cache alone.
Moved SQL server file boundary out of backups to a dedicated read-only empty directory; private bounded audit enabled, DB socket binds only internal addresses and remote port limited to web-01.

Removed embedded GitHub credential from shared Git config; root-only config now holds the credential and rotation targets it. Developers can use the original public remote URL with their own credentials; repository and release verified.

Incident: CI SSH transport matched web-01 jump on port 45844. Same CI session triggered complementary privileged archive deletes. Targeted SSH processes stopped and implicated key removed; Nico retains independent Chromebook key.
Killed matching web tunnel and removed both private key identities apparently controlled by unauthorized operator; retained independently enrolled Chromebook key for Nico.
Revoked compromised Nico SSH key prophylactically on db-01, keeping independent Chromebook key. Checking lateral-authentication records and clean local archive copies.
Verified recent encrypted DB archive opens with valid SQL-dump members, and retransmitted surviving encrypted daily archives to ci-01 without overwriting existing files.

Restricted Nico CI sudo to specific read-only operational checks and a root-owned fixed seven-day retention helper; no arbitrary privileged find or deletion. Preserved a verified database archive outside the operator cleanup path.
Host-wide key revocation on all servers; no matching lateral db-01 login found. Scheduled 17:15 payout was successful (10 sent) and manifest was accepted.

Validated new post-containment dump hash matches db-01 and placed second protected copy outside archive retention. Checked CI startup locations; no unexpected persistence or secret-read entries found.

At 17:17:15 the same outside source retried the stolen home-NUC key; sshd server-wide revocation explicitly denied it. Confirmed public website, crawler paths and customer photo output are functioning.
